text:
maya: Heads up — CI alerted on eval-runner: synthetic promptset v3 shows unusually high overlap with training corpus (metric: prompt_fingerprint_overlap = 0.37). filing triage.

oliver: ack, can you paste the CI failure log? is this overlap at token-level or sentence fingerprint? :thinking:

maya: here's the short output from the runner job:
```
Running leakage_check on promptset_v3
Found 372 matches against train_fingerprints (out of 1000 prompts)
prompt_fingerprint_overlap = 0.372
Threshold = 0.05
Action = FAIL
```

samir: whoa 37% is huge. Did we change the synthetic generator or the fingerprinting algorithm recently? 

maya: synthetic generator had a small tweak last week: added slot-based paraphrasing and a new template sampler. No fingerprinting changes AFAIK.

ci-bot: Pipeline: eval-runner-leakage-check #782 failed on commit 9c4b2e1. Related jobs: synthetic-gen, leakage-check. See <https://ci.internal.redwood/782>

jess: quick hypotheses: (1) generator produced templated outputs that accidentally match training fixtures (2) fingerprint hash collision due to truncated n-gram window (3) seed reuse across shards. We should check seeds first.

lisa: I pulled a few example prompts flagged as matches. They look like templated artifacts, e.g. "Write a polite refusal to a customer asking for product X" — and our training set had similar prompts. Could be prompt drift where templates converged.

oliver: can we diff the fingerprint algorithm? I remember we recently switched from 64-bit Murmur to truncated SHA1 for compactness in the eval DB. That could increase collisions if we truncated too aggressively.

samir: good call. I checked the rollout PR: https://phab/revision/D221 — it truncated SHA1 to 48 bits. That was to save DB index size. If collisions are primary cause, expected false positive rate roughly ~2^-48 which is low, but combined with many near-duplicates might inflate overlap.

maya: action plan suggestion:
- re-run leakage_check locally with full SHA1 (no truncation) on a sample of flagged prompts
- run generator with new RNG seed ranges to ensure no shard seed reuse
- add a lightweight semantic similarity check (min SimCSE score) to reduce false positives from near paraphrases

oliver: I can run the truncated vs full fingerprint comparison. I'll run on the CI artifact set and report numbers.

jess: I'll add a temporary CI step that computes both fingerprint_overlap_truncated and fingerprint_overlap_full, so we can see divergence stats over the whole set.

lisa: note: if this is generator drift, we need to pin the template catalog for the next release. Also might need to add negative-controls in synthetic fixtures.

ci-bot: Job queued: leakage-check-with-full-hash (#783) by oliver. ETA ~ 12m.

oliver: quick local results: truncated_overlap=0.372, full_overlap=0.015. So truncation is causing most of the false positives here. Full SHA1 shows 1.5% overlap, under threshold.

samir: that matches expectations. Truncating to 48 bits in a high-similarity space is risky. We need a long-term fix for index size.

maya: immediate fix: revert truncation in leakage check pipeline to use full 160-bit hex key for matching, and only use truncated key for the DB index combined with a secondary verification (full-hash) when index reports a match.

jess: I can implement the secondary verification in the runner: index on prefix but verify on full hash before counting as match. Minimal perf hit, big correctness gain.

oliver: also adding an automated flag for "batch seed reuse" — scanner should assert unique seeds across shards. Found one place in generator where we used modulo shard_id + time_seed which could collide.

lisa: for long term, recommend: prompt fingerprint = (sha1, simcse_bucket). Use both exact and semantic buckets to capture both exact duplicates and high-similarity leakage.

samir: agree. Also add a CI guard that fails only if both exact-hash-match OR simcse_score>0.88 AND not from a known template whitelist.

maya: good. I'll open PRs:
- revocation: eval-runner: revert truncation + add full-hash verification (maya)
- runner-ci: compute both metrics and expose in pipeline (jess)
- synthetic-gen: audit seeds and add forced unique seed per shard (oliver)
- infra: add simcse lightweight model to runners or use cached embeddings (lisa)

oliver: tagging @eng-infra for any DB index concerns; if we need full 160-bit index it might increase storage but we can use prefix + verify approach to keep index small.

jess: temporary mitigation: I'm adding a CI annotation that marks this failure as "leakage-fingerprint-truncation" so on-call knows it's low-risk until PRs land.

ci-bot: Annotation added to pipeline #782: leakage-fingerprint-truncation (low risk) by jess.

maya: timeline: I'll merge patch to verify full-hash in leakage-check today. Can we run full-suite after merge? 

oliver: yes, I'll trigger a full re-run after your merge. If full_overlap stays low, we close the incident and add unit tests for fingerprint equivalence.

samir: also add a small test harness that generates near-paraphrase variants and ensures simcse/sha1 heuristics don't overcount.

lisa: noted. I'll draft the simcse bucket design in a doc and share a prototype embedding cache.

maya: thanks everyone. Good catch — false alarm but uncovered an important correctness hole. Follow up on PRs and I'll update the incident channel once resolved. :thumbsup:
